text:
From highest to lowest, U.S. law runs: the Constitution; federal treaties and statutes (generally co-equal, with the later-in-time one controlling in a conflict, and treaties subject to the Constitution); federal regulations; then state constitutions, state statutes, state regulations, and local ordinances. Under the Supremacy Clause (Article VI), valid federal law overrides conflicting state law, but the Constitution sits above treaties and statutes, not below them, so the shared team note saying treaties and statutes can override it is incorrect. Supreme Court rulings on federal law bind all courts nationwide, while the treaty-statute ranking and the role of common law vary by context.

CONFIDENCE: 85
